# AnimateRowsSteps teardown waits on an already-destroyed grid

## Context

Grace found the destruction arm in `test/playwright/unit/grid/AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs:226` red after PR #20382. Independently reproduced on dev `f659f97390`:

```text
npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/grid/AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs:226
Symbol(Neo.isDestroyed)
1 failed
```

## The Problem

The test destroys its grid and already waits 400 ms to witness late work. Its `afterEach` then calls `await grid?.timeout(20)` before checking whether that grid is destroyed. The new already-destroyed guard in `Base#timeout` correctly rejects that extra wait. The failure is in test cleanup, not an uncaught AnimateRows step.

A temporary isolated copy changing only the teardown wait to run on a live grid passed all 8 tests. Removing the spec's historical browser-required skip also passed all 8 under `CI=1 NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=1`: this is the Node single-thread simulation and uses no browser fixture. Four adjacent grid specs with similar teardown syntax passed 43 tests; their grid is either live at teardown or the test clears its reference.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `Base#timeout` documents that destruction rejects with `Neo.isDestroyed`, including calls made after destruction. The fixture must respect that lifecycle. The genuine-error and superseded-error arms in this file must continue to exercise their reporting paths.

Prescription checked: the `afterEach` and file-level skip in `AnimateRowsSteps.spec.mjs` own this concern. No runtime behavior or public contract change is needed.

## The Fix

Guard the teardown's owned wait with grid liveness, and remove this spec's obsolete `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` browser exclusion so CI executes the destruction regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: All 8 AnimateRowsSteps tests pass locally, including destruction and genuine first-step error reporting.
- [ ] AC-2: `CI=1 NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI=1` executes and passes all 8 tests rather than skipping them.
- [ ] AC-3: The existing BaseTimeout and VdomDestroyCancellation suites remain green; no runtime cancellation contract is weakened.

## Out of Scope

Production timeout/VDOM changes and unrelated grid fixture rewrites.

## Avoided Traps

Do not swallow all teardown errors or make destroyed-owner timeouts resolve. Do not remove the explicit post-destroy wall-clock observation in the test body; it is the behavior under test.
